name: Medly AI
product: AI exam-prep tutor that marks students' practice answers (including handwriting) and gives personalised feedback for GCSE, A-level, IB and SAT.
expansion_signal: Seed funds UK growth plus international expansion; it recently launched SAT prep in the US and plans AP and ACT support by year end.
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Ghanaian and Kenyan private-school students sitting Cambridge IGCSE/A-levels, IB or the SAT for study abroad could pay a monthly fee for instant exam-style marking instead of costly private tutors.
founders: Dr Paul Jung, Dr Kavi Samra
notes: 400,000+ UK users since Feb 2025 launch; total funding about $12M. Curricula (IGCSE, A-level, IB, SAT) are already widely taken in Anglophone Africa.

name: Loora
product: Conversational AI English tutor for adults, most of whom learn English to advance their careers.
expansion_signal: Capital will accelerate go-to-market across the US, Europe, Asia and South America; headcount to double to 60 within six months.
africa_use_case: Career-focused adults in francophone and lusophone Africa (Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroon, DRC, Mozambique, Angola) need business English for jobs and could pay a subscription in local currency.
founders: Roy Mor (co-founder; other founders not confirmed)
notes: 15M+ learners, ARR in the tens of millions; total funding $43.25M. Big existing markets in Mexico, Japan, Germany and Brazil per EdSheet. Website domain not confirmed in a source during this research.

name: Sortmyprep
product: Curriculum-aligned conversational AI tutor ('Sorty') with adaptive study plans and 24x7 doubt resolution for school exams, including IB and IGCSE.
lead_investors: Not stated (angel round: Boman Irani, Sameer Mehta, Subrat Pani, Rohini Kasturi, Ranjit Pawar)
expansion_signal: Plans to expand curriculum coverage and accelerate growth across India and international markets; reported to serve students in 15+ countries.
africa_use_case: IGCSE and IB students at private schools in Lagos, Abuja, Nairobi and Accra could pay a low monthly fee for an always-on tutor aligned to their exact syllabus.
founders: Ananya, Aryaman, Naman (surnames not given in source)
notes: Small round, so a nimble partner. Global-board focus (IB/IGCSE) is a direct match for African international schools.

name: Mindmax
product: Voice-and-visual conversational AI tutor that helps people pass professional exams and learn workplace skills.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Nigerian and Kenyan professionals preparing for ACCA, ICAN, CFA, CIPS or PMP exams could pay per course or monthly for an AI coach instead of expensive tuition centres.
notes: Founded by the Memrise team (Memrise claims 35M+ users), so they know global consumer distribution. Mobile app for iPhone and Android per startuphub.

name: Eevi
product: Voice-first AI language tutor built around real-time spoken conversation rather than tap-and-swipe drills.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Professionals in Rwanda, Cameroon or Senegal switching between French and English for work, and Africans preparing to relocate to Europe, could pay a monthly fee for speaking practice.
notes: Closed beta Jan-Jun 2026 with ~100 advanced learners; 36Kr says it targets international working professionals. Very early stage.

name: Aristotle
product: Voice-first AI tutoring sold directly to families for 13-18 year olds in STEM, standardized test prep and languages.
expansion_signal: Domestic only: funds support nationwide general availability of the platform.
africa_use_case: SAT-bound secondary students and their parents in Lagos, Accra and Nairobi could pay monthly for voice tutoring in maths and test prep.
founders: Shan Reddy, Jaiden Reddy, Vivek Vajipey
notes: Original press release on PR Newswire (2026-09-16). Pre-launch, 1,000+ students completed 1,500+ tutoring hours (36Kr).

name: Arivihan
product: AI learning platform with recorded lessons, an on-demand doubt-solving agent and study plans for Indian state boards, CBSE and NEET.
pricing_model: Low-cost entry plan of Rs 51 per year; 4 lakh+ paying students (per Times of India)
expansion_signal: Domestic only: funds go to wider state-board and exam coverage, a bigger content catalogue and more language localisation within India.
africa_use_case: Its ultra-low-price model for tier-3 and rural students fits price-sensitive WAEC, NECO and KCSE candidates, though content would need African syllabi.
founders: Ritesh Singh Chandel (co-founder and CEO; others not confirmed)
notes: About 80% of subscribers are in tier-3 and rural areas (EdSheet). The pricing playbook is very close to what African mass-market students can afford.

name: BOOKR Kids
product: Interactive digital books and activities (BOOKR Class) for children's literacy and English language learning.
lead_investors: TCEE Fund IV (advised by 3TS Capital Partners)
expansion_signal: Funding targets expansion into Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas; already serves 600,000+ students in 30+ countries.
africa_use_case: Parents and low-fee private schools in Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya wanting English reading practice for young children could buy family or class subscriptions.
notes: Product is integrated with school curricula and has a teacher dashboard, so some sales are school-led. Launching BOOKR Next (ages 10-18) and BOOKR Phonics.

name: AILA
product: AI platform that finds learning gaps and personalises study paths, with AILA Tests for exam preparation aimed at Arabic-speaking students.
expansion_signal: Proceeds fund expansion into new regional and international markets and broader reach across education systems.
africa_use_case: Arabic-speaking secondary students in Egypt, Sudan, Libya and the Maghreb preparing for national exams could pay for personalised Arabic-language exam prep.
founders: Yousef Alsayed, Abdulaziz Bin Mugayel, Nouf Mugayel
notes: Also sells to schools (teacher/school-leader dashboards). Regional expansion plan makes North Africa a natural next step.

name: Astral
product: AI maths tutor for grades K-8 sold directly to families, with a curriculum that adapts to each child's pace.
pricing_model: $100 per month per family (per EdSheet); approved for ESA spending in nine US states
expansion_signal: Domestic only: aims to reach families in all 50 US states.
africa_use_case: Homeschooling and upper-income parents in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg supplementing primary maths could pay monthly, though $100/month is at the top of the affordable range.
notes: Clear direct-to-parent subscription. A lower-priced tier would be needed for most African buyers.

name: Wild Zebra
product: Socratic AI tutor for maths and reading for grades 2-9 that builds lessons around each student's interests and tracks mastery.
pricing_model: Family plan of $48 per month per child; also sold to schools
expansion_signal: Domestic only: moving from private schools into charter and public schools; funds go to engineering hires, sales and marketing.
africa_use_case: Parents of primary and junior-secondary pupils at private schools in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana could pay monthly for maths and reading tutoring at home.
notes: Consumer plan only opened this year; most usage is via private schools and the E3n/ERB channel.

name: ProLearn
product: AI-native learning companion and photo-based doubt solver for K-12 students and JEE, NEET, UPSC and CAT aspirants.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: WAEC, NECO and KCSE candidates who need step-by-step maths and science help from a photo of a problem could pay a small monthly fee if content is mapped to African syllabi.
notes: Founded April 2026 by an ex-Vedantu director; pre-launch at funding time. Google Play listing describes an NCERT/CBSE-aligned doubt solver.

name: Turing (GPAI)
product: GPAI, an AI study agent for university students covering lectures, assignments, exam prep and team projects, with reasoning and visualisation tools.
pricing_model: Freemium; previously paid features made free from September 2026
lead_investors: Not stated (investors: Korea Development Bank, Kingo Investment Partners, Company K Partners, Kolon Investment)
expansion_signal: Plans to accelerate overseas expansion and serve college students worldwide regardless of major or country; already used at 415 US universities.
africa_use_case: Engineering and science undergraduates at universities such as Lagos, Nairobi, Makerere and KNUST could pay for premium study-agent features to handle problem sets and exams.
notes: 1.5M sign-ups within a year. Making features free reduces near-term payment need; Cozzipay pitch would target future premium tiers.

name: YoLearn.ai
product: Voice-based AI tutor with an interactive whiteboard for school students and JEE/NEET aspirants, in 22 languages including Hindi and Hinglish.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Its multilingual voice tutoring could serve secondary students in Nigeria, Kenya or Tanzania who learn better in a mix of English and local languages, if African languages and syllabi are added.
notes: Separately reported a $500K raise around mid-2026 (Startuptalky, Inc42). Website taken from a search-result URL; not verified by fetch.

name: LearnVector
product: New AI-native learning company building agent-based personal tutors that drill learners until they master skills, aimed at white-collar upskilling.
expansion_signal: Coursera and LearnVector plan to explore pairing LearnVector's technology with Coursera's content library and global distribution.
africa_use_case: African professionals already paying for Coursera certificates (Nigeria, Kenya and Egypt are large Coursera markets) could buy AI-tutored upskilling courses for AI-era jobs.
notes: Coursera owns about a third. First courses expected early 2027 (Hoodline), so there is no product yet.

name: Refer
product: AI talent agent ('Lia') that represents tech job seekers and makes warm introductions to hiring managers when both sides are interested.
pricing_model: Candidate pays 20% of first month's salary only after being hired; free for employers (optional paid priority tier)
expansion_signal: Domestic only: expanded from Stanford new grads to all tech workers and employers nationwide.
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Kenyan and Ghanaian software engineers chasing remote US roles could use the no-upfront-cost model and settle the success fee from their wallet in local currency.
notes: Rare career tool where the job seeker is the paying customer. Worker-paid placement fees face legal limits in some countries (ILO C181), so check regulation per market.

name: Coding Giants
product: Coding, maths and STEM courses for children and teenagers, sold to families across 13 markets.
round_amount_usd: Up to EUR 6M (USD not stated in source)
expansion_signal: Debt will fund expansion beyond Europe into the US, Mexico and Spain, including through acquisitions.
africa_use_case: Middle-class parents in Lagos, Nairobi and Accra already pay for after-school coding clubs and could buy online coding courses for their children.
notes: Known in Poland as Giganci Programowania; 130,000+ learners and about $15M ARR (EdSheet). Debt rather than equity; earlier EUR 8.5M equity round was Dec 2024.

name: SpeakX
product: Generative-AI app for practising spoken English through real-life conversation scenarios with personalised feedback.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Job seekers in francophone Africa and in Ethiopia who need confident spoken English for interviews and BPO jobs could pay a small monthly fee.
notes: Formerly Yellow Class; raised $16M led by WestBridge in Oct 2025. Inc42 records $23.3M total across 4 rounds. The Sept 2026 deal is an undisclosed celebrity angel investment.

name: Artwod
product: Guided drawing lessons ('Learning Roads') plus community critique that help visual artists improve their skills.
expansion_signal: None stated (funds launch a creators' marketplace and grow community participation)
africa_use_case: Aspiring illustrators, comic artists and animators in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg's growing creative scenes could pay for structured drawing courses and portfolio feedback.
notes: Creative-skills learning; the planned creators' marketplace could also need payouts and pay-ins.

name: ArtMaster (Artie)
product: Artie, an AI piano-learning app that listens to a user's playing, spots errors and generates tailored exercises.
lead_investors: Not stated (investors: Factorial Capital, Reflex Capital, Moises, Nir Zicherman, Grant Davis, Eliska Vorel)
expansion_signal: None stated (product expansion only: guitar support and an Android version)
africa_use_case: Church keyboardists and young musicians across Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya could pay a monthly subscription once the Android version ships.
notes: Currently iOS-first; the Android launch matters for African reach.

name: Jack & Jill
hq_country: United Kingdom / United States (London and San Francisco)
product: Two AI agents: 'Jack' represents job seekers and 'Jill' represents employers, and introductions happen only when both sides opt in.
expansion_signal: Scaling across the US after launches in San Francisco and New York; lead investor describes the goal as a better global talent marketplace.
africa_use_case: Experienced African tech talent seeking international or remote roles could use 'Jack'; payment would come from any future premium candidate tier.
notes: 380,000 job seekers and 5,000+ employers (EdSheet). Revenue appears to come mostly from employers, so the pay-in need is weaker.

name: HiringCafe
product: Job search engine that scrapes company career pages directly, plus a free AI Talent Agent that matches uploaded resumes to open roles and filters ghost jobs.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African job seekers hunting remote global roles could use it today; Cozzipay matters only if premium job-seeker features launch.
notes: 2M monthly active users built organically. No paid consumer product confirmed.

name: Roleo
product: Personal AI career agent that watches the job market for tech professionals and connects them directly with hiring companies.
expansion_signal: Funding will take the career agent to tech professionals across Europe.
africa_use_case: African developers seeking European remote or relocation roles could benefit, but payment use depends on future paid tiers.
notes: Founded by a Veriff co-founder and an ex-Wise engineer. Plans to support users across their whole professional lives.

name: Fika Jobs
product: Video-first hiring platform where AI agents interview candidates to create pre-assessed profiles that employers can search.
expansion_signal: None stated (preparing a wider public launch later in 2026)
africa_use_case: African graduates applying to European employers could show soft skills through AI video interviews rather than CVs; payment fit depends on a candidate-paid tier.
notes: Backed by King co-founders. Pre-launch at funding time; business model not disclosed.

name: Matiks
product: Competitive mental-maths, logic, memory and puzzle game app where users duel bots and real players.
pricing_model: Freemium; testing a subscription (analysis, tips, practice) plus in-app purchases
expansion_signal: Funding to expand into new markets; seeing traction in the US, South Korea and Japan and plans localisation for the latter two.
africa_use_case: Students and young adults in Nigeria and Kenya, where maths competitions and olympiads are popular, could buy the subscription or in-app boosts for practice.
founders: Sudhanshu Bhatia, Mohan Kumar, Sushant Timmapur
notes: Borderline education: positioned as mind-sports gaming. 2.2M MAU in Sept 2026. In-app purchases are a natural fit for one-click wallet payments.

name: Kollegio
product: Free AI college counsellor that helps students with school matching, essays, scholarships and application planning.
pricing_model: Free for students; revenue from college partners (per EdSheet)
lead_investors: Not stated (investors: Reach Capital, JFF Ventures, ECMC Group, Workshop Venture Partners, Alumni Ventures, Dent Capital, AiSprouts VC)
expansion_signal: None stated (plans to broaden into general education and career planning)
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Ghanaian and Kenyan students applying to US colleges and scholarships need exactly this guidance; any paid essay or premium tier could be paid via Cozzipay.
notes: 300,000+ student users. Free to students, so the pay-in need is weak today. Round month from Preqin (October 2026).

name: Ed.ai
product: AI assistant that helps teachers grade student work, analyse learning gaps and create personalised remediation, focused on secondary maths.
expansion_signal: Funds expansion into the US and other European markets plus entry into higher education.
africa_use_case: Secondary maths teachers in francophone Africa (Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroon) who follow French-style curricula and grade large classes could pay for a personal teacher subscription.
notes: Unclear whether teachers can buy self-serve or whether sales go through schools; verify before pitching. French-language product suits francophone Africa.

name: Bloomy
product: Adaptive K-12 maths, English and writing curriculum taught by a Socratic AI tutor that requires mastery before students advance.
lead_investors: Not stated (investors: Reach Capital, Rethink Capital Partners, Silicon Schools Fund, Workshop Venture Partners, Y Combinator, Robinhood, Transpose Platform)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Parents and low-cost private schools in Nigeria and Kenya looking for mastery-based maths and English could subscribe per child.
notes: YC S26. Sells to schools and families, but traction so far is mainly in schools (e.g. a California charter school). Website from apis.io listing.

name: Lytmus AI
product: AI 'teacher twin' mentors trained on top educators' styles, giving round-the-clock help to NEET medical-entrance aspirants.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: The teacher-twin model could serve Nigerian students preparing for JAMB/post-UTME medicine, but content is NEET-specific today.
notes: Original report in Business Standard (2026-06-28). Narrow India exam focus.

name: Vidyakul
product: Hindi-first vernacular learning platform with courses and AI-powered academic support for Indian state-board students.
round_amount_usd: INR 10 crore (USD not stated in source)
expansion_signal: Domestic only: expanding beyond Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to more Indian states.
africa_use_case: Its local-language model could be copied for Hausa-, Swahili- or Amharic-medium secondary learners, but current content is India-only.
founders: Tarun Saini, Raman Garg (co-founders); Akhil Hari Angira (co-founder, CBO)
notes: Debt from a foundation rather than an equity round. Announced one day before the research cut-off.

name: Archer (formerly hackajob)
hq_country: United Kingdom / United States (London and New York)
product: AI recruiting agent that matches job seekers to roles they fit and automates candidate sourcing and qualification for employers.
expansion_signal: Funds expansion of go-to-market teams in New York and London.
africa_use_case: African engineers seeking UK and US tech roles could use the job-seeker agent, but revenue comes from enterprise recruiters, so wallet demand is low.
notes: About 120 enterprise customers; mostly employer-paid, so it is borderline on the self-serve criterion. Included as a low-priority lead.

name: AMentoria
product: Online prep courses plus one-to-one mentoring by successful students for competitive Brazilian university entrance exams, especially medicine.
lead_investors: Triaxis Capital, Crescera Capital (FIP Nordeste Capital Semente)
expansion_signal: Domestic only: new operations in Sao Paulo and other Brazilian regions; scaling a B2B2C model with schools.
africa_use_case: The peer-mentoring model could appeal to Portuguese-speaking pre-med students in Angola and Mozambique, but content is tied to Brazil's ENEM.
founders: Pedro Gesteira, Alvaro Figueiredo, Matheus Gomes
notes: Weakest fit on Africa scalability; included to reach the target count. Original source: startups.com.br.
